terms.meaning: a library for drawing charts in React
a small box that appears when the mouse rests over part of a chart, showing its values
a key that matches colors on a chart to the names of the data series
a set of colors for one mode, such as light or dark
a named color or value stored in the page's styles so many elements can share it
a React feature that inserts raw markup into the page without checking it, so the content must be trusted

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for charts
sections.what: Loads React, the recharts charting library and the class-joining helper. Nothing is shown on its own.
sections.why: The file builds on recharts, so it needs those parts.

sections.name: THEMES
sections.title: Light and dark theme selectors
sections.what: Lists the two themes and the selector each one uses. Light has no selector, and dark uses the dark class.
sections.why: Lets each series have its own color in each theme.
sections.watch_out: The dark selector must match the class the app uses to switch to dark mode, or dark colors will not apply.

sections.name: ChartConfig
sections.title: Configuration shape
sections.what: Defines what each data series entry may contain: a label, an icon, and either one color or one color per theme.
sections.why: Gives one place to describe how each series looks and is named.
sections.watch_out: Keys in the configuration must match the data names exactly, or the chart falls back to raw names.

sections.name: ChartContextProps
sections.title: Shared chart channel
sections.what: Creates the channel that passes the configuration to the chart parts beneath it, so they do not need it passed by hand.
sections.why: Avoids passing the same settings through many layers.
sections.watch_out: Chart parts used outside the chart container receive no configuration.

sections.name: useChart
sections.title: Chart container and lookup
sections.what: Provides the lookup that gives chart parts their configuration and raises an error if used outside the container. The container wraps the chart with a unique id, color rules, and a box that sizes the chart to fit.
sections.why: Likely reason: the unique id keeps the styles of several charts on one page from clashing. Reason otherwise not stated.
sections.watch_out: The chart sizes itself to its parent, so the parent must have a real width or the chart may not show.

sections.name: ChartStyle (part 1)
sections.title: Theme color rules
sections.what: Creates a hidden style block that sets a color for each series in each theme, limited to this chart's id. It also gives the standard tooltip a project name.
sections.why: Lets each chart take its colors from the configuration instead of fixed colors in the chart code.
sections.watch_out: Colors are placed into the page without escaping, so they must come from trusted code, never from user input.

sections.name: ChartStyle (part 2)
sections.title: Tooltip setup and title
sections.what: Starts the hover box: reads the configuration, works out the title to show at the top, and reuses that work until the data changes.
sections.why: Computes the title once so the box does not redo the work on every mouse move.
sections.watch_out: The title is looked up by label key first, so a missing label setting can show the raw name instead of a friendly label.

sections.name: ChartStyle (part 3)
sections.title: Tooltip show-or-hide and layout
sections.what: Draws the title and hides the whole box when nothing is hovered. It decides whether the title sits above the rows or inside the first row, based on whether there is one item and whether the indicator is a dot.
sections.why: Likely reason: a single item reads more clearly with its name inline. Reason otherwise not stated.
sections.watch_out: The box is hidden whenever the chart reports no activity, so a chart that does not report hover will never show it.

sections.name: ChartStyle (part 4)
sections.title: Each row in the tooltip
sections.what: For each item in the hover box, shows either the page's custom display or a colored marker, then the name, then the value with thousands separators.
sections.why: Shows each series clearly with the matching color.
sections.watch_out: The value check treats zero as missing in a way that shows a loose zero digit instead of a formatted value.

sections.name: ChartStyle (part 5)
sections.title: Close tooltip and start legend
sections.what: Closes the hover box, gives the legend a project name, and starts the legend. The legend draws nothing when there are no entries.
sections.why: Hides the legend when no series data is present.
sections.watch_out: The top or bottom setting here only adds spacing; the chart library decides where the legend sits.

sections.name: ChartStyle (part 6)
sections.title: Legend entries
sections.what: Draws each legend entry as a small colored square, or as the series icon, followed by its label.
sections.why: Lets readers match colors on the chart with the series names.
sections.watch_out: The legend color comes from the chart's own series color, not from the configuration, so the two can disagree if the data and configuration differ.

sections.name: getPayloadConfigFromPayload
sections.title: Finding a series settings
sections.what: Looks up the settings for one data series. It checks the data entry for a matching key first, then the nested data, and falls back to the configuration key by name.
sections.why: Series names in the data may not match the configuration keys, so this links the two.
sections.watch_out: If no match is found, the label falls back to the raw series name.

summary: Helpers that wrap the recharts library so charts get consistent colors, hover boxes, legends and light or dark theme support.
purpose: Lets the app draw charts that match its look, with colors and labels set from one configuration object.
why: Likely reason: keeps chart styling in one place on top of the recharts library. Reason not stated for specific choices.
how: Step 1: Defines the light and dark themes and the shape of the chart configuration. Step 2: Provides a shared channel that gives chart parts the configuration. Step 3: Wraps the chart in a container that sets a unique id and inserts color rules. Step 4: Builds the hover box and its rows. Step 5: Builds the legend and its entries. Step 6: Finds the settings for each data series by name.
inputs: A configuration object giving each data series a label, an icon, and a color or a per-theme color, plus the chart itself and any tooltip or legend settings.
outputs: A styled chart with hover boxes and legend entries on screen.
risks: Colors are inserted into the page as raw text with no checking, so untrusted color values could insert unwanted markup. A zero value shows as a loose zero in the hover box. Series names must match configuration keys exactly.
debug: If colors are missing, check that each series has a color or a theme color and that the chart id is set. If dark mode colors are wrong, check that the dark selector matches the app's dark mode class. If a label shows a raw data name, check the configuration key spelling. If a hover box shows a stray zero, see the row value check.
